findings.evidence: The diff adds `@[expose] def dimensionShiftUp ... := cokernel ...` and `@[expose] def dimensionShiftUpSES ... := ShortComplex.cokernelSequence ...`; their own docstrings confirm that public `dimensionShiftUpSES_def`, `_X₁`, and `_X₃` lemmas already expose the required identifications.
findings.fix: Remove both `@[expose]` annotations and state the dimension-shift connecting-map API using the existing endpoint equalities (or add a dedicated transported endpoint/connecting-map lemma), so consumers do not unfold either definition.
findings.issue: `@[expose]` on `dimensionShiftUp` and, at line 101, `dimensionShiftUpSES` exposes cokernel/short-complex implementations solely to make the new endpoint types definitionally reduce; this creates an unstable public interface despite existing `_def` and `_X₁`/`_X₃` characterization lemmas.

summary: The new cohomology API unnecessarily exposes two implementation bodies, making downstream code depend on definitional reduction instead of the existing characteristic API.
